acceptance_criteria: AC-1 The test passes against the two contracts as they stand today.
AC-2 Removing a clause from either section fails the test; a test fixture or a temporary-file variant proves it rather than an edit to the real document.
AC-3 Adding a clause fails it, and reordering two clauses fails it.
AC-4 Rewording a clause's explanation without changing its identifier or position does NOT fail it.
AC-5 The failure message names the document, the section, the expectation and the finding, and says that changing a frozen shape is a Product Owner decision.
AC-6 The new test and tests/test_contract_authority_status.py pass, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_C7_BACKUP_ARTEFACT_RESTORE_ENGINE_CONTRACT.md and docs/design/UI2_0_C2_JOB_EXECUTION_CONTRACT.md, both FROZEN. A FROZEN document is authority level 2 in AGENTS.md's hierarchy: implementation is written against it and a reviewer trusts it has not changed. The contract-status law requires every contract-bearing document to state its status; nothing yet requires the content behind that status to stay put. This movement adds no rule -- it makes an existing one checkable.

report.objective: Stop a frozen contract drifting in content while its status line still reads FROZEN. The test tree pins contract STATUSES -- that a document says FROZEN -- and nothing pins the SHAPE of what it froze. A clause can be added, removed or reordered inside a FROZEN document and every gate stays green. This movement pins the shape of the two clause lists that gate the most dangerous behaviour in the product.
output_contract: A frozen contract that changes shape fails the build instead of passing quietly.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One text-reading test over two named sections; the hard part is pinning shape without pinning prose, and the predecessor's failure says exactly what to avoid.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every command runs from the repository root.
Run only the commands named above plus your own new test file.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before every commit and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE states the shape you pinned for each section -- how many clauses and their identifiers -- and what you deliberately did not pin.
risks: Copying the superseded test's counts instead of reading today's text, which reproduces exactly the failure that kept it out of the tree.
Pinning sentence wording, which makes every future clarification a test failure and trains people to edit the guard.
Anchoring on line numbers, which any edit above the section silently breaks.
Editing a contract to make the test pass, which inverts the whole point.

in: One test that reads the two documents as text, extracts the clause list under each of the two named sections, and asserts its shape: how many clauses there are, and their identifiers or leading labels in order. Derive both from the current text -- read it, do not assume a count.
Pin the shape, not the prose. A clause's explanatory sentences may be improved without failing the test; adding, removing or reordering a clause must fail it.

The failure message must say what a reader needs in order to act: which document, which section, what was expected and what was found, and that changing a frozen contract's shape is a Product Owner decision rather than a test to update.
A short comment in the test saying why it exists: a FROZEN status line is a claim about content, and this is what makes the claim checkable.
out: Editing either contract. Not one character. If the current text looks wrong, say so in the SESSION_CLOSE and leave it.
Importing or adapting tests/test_ui2_d1_restore_admission_contract.py from pull request #180.
Pinning any other document, or widening the guard to every contract in the tree. Two sections, named above.
Pinning prose, sentence wording or punctuation; a test that fails on an improved explanation is worse than no test.
